more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Polyglycerol esters combine short polyglycerol chains with fatty acids from edible fats and oils; the composition is a mixture rather than one molecule. Its emulsifying role is to help form or maintain mixtures of oil and water in the finished food. Made by esterifying polyglycerol with edible fats, oils or their fatty acids. The polyglycerol component mainly contains short chains of glycerol units. The specified material is supplied as yellow liquid or waxy solid.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; sweet baked goods; breakfast cereals.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Made by esterifying polyglycerol with edible fats, oils or their fatty acids. The polyglycerol component mainly contains short chains of glycerol units.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The fatty-acid feedstock is not specified as exclusively plant derived. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher suitability cannot be established without the supplier identifying the raw material and processing.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern for assessed food uses.
A limited three-week human study reported no adverse findings at larger intakes.
